Jordan: Hi folks, I'm prepping my first PR (small router tweak + unit test). Quick runbook: what's the preferred way to split changes when touching runtime + tests? Don't want to make it huge.

Priya: Welcome Jordan! If the change is a single logical update (runtime change + its tests) keep it in one PR. If you're changing APIs or adding a new public config, split into two: infra change first, then usage.

Nina: For size, we usually aim for <300 LOC of real code. Large test fixtures can bloat lines; try to factor helpers into test util files. If it's >500 LOC please add a short note in the PR body explaining the rationale.

Jordan: Good call. Any PR template checklist I should fill out?

devx: PR template lives at https://git.redwood.example/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Quick checklist: 1) link ticket 2) describe change & rollback plan 3) mention CODEOWNERS 4) perf/regression notes if applicable 5) tests added & how to run.

Jordan: Rollback plan? Example format?

Priya: Simple bullets work. Eg: "Rollback: revert PR, redeploy, flush cache via `tools/cachectl invalidate --prefix=route-*`". For perf-sensitive changes add a metric to monitor (latency or p99) and who to alert.

Nina: Commit messages: `area(scope): brief summary` e.g., `runtime(router): reduce cold start locks`. Add the ticket ID at end if not in branch name. We prefer squashed merges for small fixes; keep history for multi-commit features.

Jordan: Good. Pre-commit/lint? CI?

ops-bot: Pre-commit checks configured. Current repo hooks: black, isort, mypy, flake8. CI blocks merge on failures. Link: https://ci.redwood.example/job/1749994321

Priya: Run `make dev-setup` to install hooks and `pre-commit run --all-files` before pushing. If tests are flaky locally, run `make test -k <pattern>` or ask me and I'll help reproduce.

Jordan: Anything about reviewers and approvals?

Nina: Add 2 reviewers: one codeowner for the area and one peer. For runtime changes that could impact latency, ping @performance-reviewers and add `needs-perf` label. CODEOWNERS enforces at least one approval from owners.

Priya: If the PR touches generated files (eg. schema outputs), include a note and run `scripts/generate.sh` so CI doesn't fail. Don't commit compiled binaries.

Jordan: One more: branching naming convention?

devx: Use `feature/<ticket>-short-desc` or `fix/<ticket>-short-desc`. Keep it under 50 chars after the ticket slug. Example: `feature/ENG-412-router-debounce`.

Jordan: Thanks all. I'll open the PR and paste the link here. Appreciate the hand-holding for the first one. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: CI reported 2 flaky tests on main yesterday; if you hit them tag `flake` label and ping @eng-oncall.

Jordan: Noted — will do if CI flakes. Opening PR now: https://git.redwood.example/pull/2345

Nina: Reviewing now, will focus on correctness + test coverage. Priya will look at ops/rollback bits.

Priya: quick nit: please add a one-line perf note in the PR body about expected change to p50/p95 even if negligible.

Jordan: Done — updated PR body. Thanks! :thumbsup:
